name: Cohen's d, posttest-only between-group design (Eq. 3)
variables: Mean_MT, Mean_ST = posttest means of the multiple-talker (treatment) and single-talker (comparison) groups; SD_pooled = pooled within-group SD (Eq. 4)
notes: Positive d means MT training is better. Engine: effect_sizes.smd(m1, sd1, n1, m2, sd2, n2, correct=False) returns uncorrected d.

name: Pooled standard deviation (Eq. 4)
variables: n_MT, n_ST = group sample sizes; SD_MT, SD_ST = group standard deviations
notes: The source's wording 'pooled standard deviation of the two group means' means the pooled within-group SD.

name: Hedges small-sample correction factor (Eq. 5)
variables: df = degrees of freedom (between-group design: n_MT + n_ST - 2; within-group change score: n - 1)
notes: Approximation to Hedges' (1981) exact J(df) = Gamma(df/2) / ( sqrt(df/2) * Gamma((df-1)/2) ). Engine default j_method='exact'; hedges_j(df, method='approx') reproduces Eq. 5. Differences are negligible except at very small df.

name: Hedges' g (Eq. 6)
variables: d = Cohen's d (Eq. 3); c(df) = correction factor (Eq. 5)
notes: Engine: effect_sizes.smd(..., correct=True, j_method='approx') matches the source's approximation; default j_method='exact'.

name: Sampling variance labelled 'variance of Hedges' g' as printed (Eq. 7)
variables: g = Hedges' g; N = total sample size; n~ = n_MT*n_ST/N; c(df) = correction factor (Eq. 5); df = N - 2
notes: Known issues (extraction notes' recomputation): the source calls n~ 'the harmonic mean' but it is half the harmonic mean (1/n~ = 1/n_MT + 1/n_ST); since (N-2)/(N-4) = df/(df-2), the expression is Hedges' (1981) exact variance of the UNCORRECTED d with delta estimated by g, not Var(g). Requires N > 4. Not implemented in the engine (effect_sizes.smd offers vtype 'LS', 'LS2', 'UB'). State which variance is used.

name: Exact sampling variance of Hedges' g (Hedges 1981)
variables: delta = population SMD (estimated by g); df = n_MT + n_ST - 2; n~ = n_MT*n_ST/(n_MT + n_ST); c(df) = correction factor
notes: Not printed in the source; given in the extraction notes as the correct counterpart of Eq. 7 (Var(g) = c^2 * Var(d)). Differs from Eq. 7 by roughly 5-10% at typical small n. Not implemented in the engine.

name: Large-sample variance of the standardised mean difference
variables: n1, n2 = group sample sizes; g = Hedges' g
notes: Not used by the source; the extraction notes cite it as the common approximation that differs from Eq. 7, so the engine must document its choice. Engine default effect_sizes.smd(vtype='LS') = this formula (metafor default).

name: Morris (2008) pretest-posttest-control Hedges' g (Eq. 8)
variables: Mean_post,MT, Mean_pre,MT = posttest and pretest means of the MT group; Mean_post,ST, Mean_pre,ST = same for the ST group; SD_pre,pooled = pooled pretest SD (Eq. 9); c(df) = correction factor
notes: df is not redefined in the source; in Morris's d_ppc2 it is n_MT + n_ST - 2. Raw-score metric (pretest SD), so it can be combined with posttest-only g under the Morris & DeShon (2002) conditions. Not implemented in the engine; compute externally.

name: Pooled pretest standard deviation (Eq. 9)
variables: SD_pre,MT, SD_pre,ST = pretest SDs of the MT and ST groups; n_MT, n_ST = group sizes
notes: Pretest SDs are preferred because they are unaffected by treatment and more consistent across studies (Becker, 1988). Engine: pooled_sd applied to the pretest SDs.

name: Sampling variance for the pretest-posttest-control design as printed (Eq. 10)
variables: rho = pre-post correlation (printed as 'p'; imputed as .7 when unreported); n_MT, n_ST = group sizes; g_MT, g_ST = within-group standardised mean changes (not defined in the source; extraction notes' reading); c(n-1) = correction factor with df = n - 1
notes: This is the sum of two Becker (1988) single-group change-score variances, not Morris's variance for d_ppc2, so the point estimate (Eq. 8) and the variance come from different estimators; flag it. Requires n > 3 per group. Not implemented in the engine. The variance that matches the Morris estimator is given in F-ZHA22-026.

name: Composite of m correlated outcomes within a study (Borenstein et al. 2009, ch. 24)
expression: Y_bar = (1/m) * sum_j y_j ;  Var(Y_bar) = (1/m)^2 * [ sum_j v_j + sum_{j != l} r * sqrt(v_j * v_l) ] ;  m = 2: Var = 0.25*(v1 + v2 + 2*r*sqrt(v1*v2))
variables: y_j = effect size of outcome j; v_j = its variance; m = number of outcomes; r = assumed correlation between outcomes (tutorial: .5, varied .25-.75)
notes: Background formula from the extraction notes (Borenstein et al. 2009 ch. 24); the source only names the method and applies it via MAd::agg with r = .5. Not implemented in the engine; aggregate before input.

name: Inverse-variance weighted summary effect
expression: w_i = 1 / v_i ;  ES_bar = sum_i (w_i * ES_i) / sum_i w_i
variables: w_i = weight of study i; v_i = its variance; ES_i = effect size of study i; ES_bar = summary effect
notes: Source states weight = 1/variance. Under random effects the weight is 1/(v_i + tau^2) (background). Engine: models.meta_analysis(model='fixed' or 'random').

name: Cochran's Q (Eq. 2)
expression: Q = sum_i w_i * (ES_i - ES_bar)^2 ;  Q ~ chi-square(k - 1) under homogeneity
variables: w_i = inverse-variance weight; ES_i = effect of study i; ES_bar = fixed-effect weighted mean; k = number of studies
notes: Example: Q = 83.85, df = 21, p < .0001 (k = 22); Q = 17.45, df = 18, p = .4926 after removing outliers (k = 19).

name: I^2 (Eq. 1)
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; k = number of studies
notes: Thresholds 25/50/75% = small/moderate/high (Higgins et al., 2003). Example: (83.85 - 21)/83.85 = 75.0%. Note: these bands are rough conventions, not absolute rules; I^2 depends on study precision (Cochrane Handbook v6 uses overlapping bands: 0-40%, 30-60%, 50-90%, 75-100%).

name: H and H^2
expression: H = sqrt(Q / df) ;  H^2 = Q / df = 1 / (1 - I^2)
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; df = k - 1 (or residual df in meta-regression); I^2 as a proportion
notes: meta prints H (example H = 2.00); metafor's meta-regression prints H^2 as unaccounted (residual) variability divided by sampling variability. Engine: models.heterogeneity returns H2 (= Q/df); H is its square root.

name: Higgins & Thompson (2002) test-based CI for H and I^2
expression: if Q > k: SE(ln H) = 0.5*(ln Q - ln(k-1)) / (sqrt(2Q) - sqrt(2k - 3)); else: SE(ln H) = sqrt( 1/(2(k-2)) * (1 - 1/(3(k-2)^2)) ) ;  CI_H = exp( ln H +/- 1.96*SE(ln H) ), bounds floored at 1 ;  I^2 bound = (H^2 - 1)/H^2, floored at 0
variables: Q = Cochran's Q; k = number of studies; H = sqrt(Q/(k-1))
notes: Higgins & Thompson (2002) test-based method, as implemented by the engine. The source does not name the CI method for I^2 and H; recomputation shows the printed k = 22 values I^2 = 75.0% [62.1, 83.5] and H = 2.00 [1.62, 2.46] reproduce exactly. Variant: meta centres the interval at ln(max(H, 1)); this differs only when Q < k - 1 (H < 1). For k = 19, Q = 17.45 meta's variant gives the printed H = 1.00 [1.00, 1.40] and I^2 = 0.0% [0.0, 48.9], whereas models.i2_ci_higgins_thompson (centred at ln H) gives upper limits of 1.38 and 47.3% (checked).

name: Wald (z-based) CI and test for the pooled mean
expression: CI = mu_hat +/- 1.96 * SE(mu_hat) ;  z = mu_hat / SE(mu_hat)
variables: mu_hat = pooled estimate; SE(mu_hat) = its standard error
notes: Used for the main random-effects analysis (g = 0.468 [0.038, 0.898], z = 2.13). Engine: models.meta_analysis(ci_method='z'); engine default for random effects is 'hksj' (background: recommended by Cochrane Handbook v6).

name: Knapp-Hartung t and F tests in meta-regression
expression: t_j = b_j / SE(b_j) ~ t(k - p) ;  single moderator: F(1, k - p) = t^2
variables: b_j = coefficient j; SE(b_j) = Knapp-Hartung-adjusted SE; k = number of studies; p = number of model coefficients incl. intercept
notes: Inferred from the t/F output of metafor::rma (test = 'knha'). Consistency check: 1.434^2 = 2.056 (printed F = 2.055, df 1 and 11); (-0.091/0.175)^2 = 0.27 (printed F = 0.269, df 1 and 13). Engine: moderators.meta_regression(test='knha').

name: R^2 analog in meta-regression (proportion of heterogeneity explained)
variables: tau^2_0 = between-study variance of the intercept-only model; tau^2_res = residual between-study variance with moderators
notes: The source gives only the definition ('amount of heterogeneity accounted for') and shows 0.00% when tau^2 is not reduced; no formula is printed. Example: R^2 = 39.14% (training length), 0.00% (presentation format).

name: Predicted effect from a meta-regression
expression: y_hat = b0 + b1 * x ;  categorical example: g_intermixed = 0.289 - 0.091 = 0.198
variables: b0 = intercept (effect at x = 0, or at the reference category); b1 = slope or category difference; x = moderator value or dummy code
notes: Continuous example: g increases by 0.052 per training hour; intercept 0.033 is the predicted g at 0 hours (meaningless without centring). The engine has no prediction function: take b0 and b1 from moderators.meta_regression and compute the prediction by hand.

name: Centring a continuous moderator
variables: x = moderator value; mean(x) = average across included studies
notes: After centring the intercept is the expected effect for a study with the average moderator value; the slope is unchanged. Engine: centre the column before passing it to moderators.meta_regression.

name: Egger regression test for funnel asymmetry (dmetar::eggers.test output)
expression: y_i/SE_i = b0 + b1*(1/SE_i) + e_i  (OLS) ;  t = b0 / SE(b0), df = k - 2 ;  dmetar CI = b0 +/- 1.96*SE(b0)
variables: y_i = effect size of study i; SE_i = its standard error; b0 = intercept (0 expected without asymmetry); SE(b0) = its standard error; k = number of studies
notes: Expected intercept 0. Example: b0 = 1.959, t = 2.277, p = .0339, CI [0.27, 3.64] (k = 22). The regression, t and p are what bias.egger_test implements; the CI convention is not printed in the source - recomputation shows dmetar uses the normal quantile 1.96, while bias.egger_test uses the t(k-2) quantile and so gives about [0.16, 3.75] here. Use only with at least 10 studies (Sterne et al., 2011). For SMDs the classic test has inflated Type I error because g and SE are correlated; prefer a sample-size-based precision (Pustejovsky & Rodgers, 2019).

name: Outlier rule of dmetar::find.outliers
expression: outlier_i  <=>  upper_i < lower_pooled  OR  lower_i > upper_pooled ;  [lower_i, upper_i] = y_i +/- 1.96*sqrt(v_i)
variables: y_i, v_i = effect and variance of study i; [lower_pooled, upper_pooled] = 95% CI of the pooled random-effects estimate
notes: Background: this is dmetar's documented rule; the source only says that the flagged studies' CIs do not overlap the summary estimate in the forest plot. Heuristic; not implemented as such in the engine (effect_sizes.study_ci gives the study CI; sensitivity.influence flags |rstudent| > 1.96). Removing flagged studies is a post hoc sensitivity analysis, not the primary result.

name: Influence cut-offs (metafor defaults)
expression: influential if |DFFITS| > 3*sqrt(p/(k - p))  OR  Cook's D > median of chi-square(p)  OR  hat > 3p/k  OR  any |DFBETAS| > 1
variables: p = number of model coefficients (1 for an intercept-only model); k = number of studies
notes: Background: the source prints no numeric cut-offs. The extraction notes also list 'covariance ratio < 1'; in metafor a COVRATIO below 1 only indicates that removing the study improves precision and is not one of the flagging rules (the engine flags by the four rules above).

name: Random-effects power of the pooled test (dmetar::power.analysis)
expression: v_d = (n1 + n2)/(n1*n2) + d^2/(2(n1 + n2)) ;  v_m = (v_d / k) * f ;  lambda = d / sqrt(v_m) ;  power = 1 - Phi(z_{1-alpha/2} - lambda) + Phi(-z_{1-alpha/2} - lambda)
variables: d = expected effect size; n1, n2 = average group sizes; k = expected number of studies; f = heterogeneity multiplier (1 fixed, 1.33 low, 1.67 moderate, 2 high); alpha = significance level; Phi = standard normal CDF
notes: Background (dmetar implementation), not printed in the source, which only shows the call power.analysis(d = 0.7, k = 18, n1 = 15, n2 = 15, p = .05, heterogeneity = 'moderate') with power above 90%. Not implemented in the engine.

name: Sampling variance of the Morris (2008) pretest-posttest-control estimator d_ppc2 (background)
expression: Var(g_ppc2) = 2*c(df)^2*(1 - rho)*((n_MT + n_ST)/(n_MT*n_ST))*((n_MT + n_ST - 2)/(n_MT + n_ST - 4))*(1 + delta^2 / (2*(1 - rho)*(n_MT + n_ST)/(n_MT*n_ST))) - delta^2 ,  df = n_MT + n_ST - 2
variables: rho = pre-post correlation; n_MT, n_ST = group sizes; c(df) = small-sample correction (Eq. 5); delta = population pretest-posttest-control effect, estimated by g from Eq. 8
notes: Not printed in the source: it is Morris's own variance for the estimator of Eq. 8, given here because the source's Eq. 10 (a sum of two Becker single-group variances) does not belong to that estimator. Structure: Hedges' exact variance with 1/n~ replaced by 2(1 - rho)(n_MT + n_ST)/(n_MT n_ST). Requires n_MT + n_ST > 4. Like Eq. 10 it depends on the imputed rho (.7 in the tutorial), so vary rho in a sensitivity analysis. Not implemented in the engine.

name: Random-effects prediction interval (background; missing from the source)
variables: mu_hat = random-effects pooled estimate; SE(mu_hat) = its standard error; tau^2 = between-study variance; k = number of studies
locator: p. 10 (inputs only; the PI itself is not in the source)
notes: Background (Higgins, Thompson & Spiegelhalter 2009; recommended by Cochrane Handbook v6 and IntHout et al. 2016). Applied to the printed k = 22 values (mu = 0.468, SE about 0.219 from the CI, tau^2 = 0.8240): about [-1.48, 2.42] (recomputed), which shows how widely the true effects may vary despite the significant mean. Engine: models.meta_analysis(pi_method='t_k-2'), the default.
